pipelinesSetup.cloud.title: Connect a cloud
pipelinesSetup.cloud.intro: Bemmoly reads and deploys only where you allow it. Connecting creates nothing in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.gcpServices: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.vmHint: Uses that VM's service account. No key files.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.gcloud: My gcloud sign-in on this machine
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.gcloudHint: For a laptop install. Acts as you.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.signIn.wifHint: For Bemmoly running outside Google Cloud.

pipelinesSetup.cloud.connected: Google Cloud connected. Nothing was created.
pipelinesSetup.cloud.name: Google Cloud
pipelinesSetup.wif.consoleLink: Get it from the Google Cloud console
pipelinesSetup.wif.notJson: That file is not JSON. Choose the file the console downloaded.
pipelinesSetup.wif.isKey: That is a service account key. Bemmoly never takes keys; make a workload identity file instead.
pipelinesSetup.wif.notFederation: That is not a workload identity file. Its type should be external_account.
pipelinesSetup.wif.onVm: Bemmoly on a Google Cloud VM? Choose 'The machine Bemmoly runs on' instead; no file needed.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step1: IAM and admin › Workload Identity Federation › Create pool, named bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step2: Add a provider for where Bemmoly runs: OpenID Connect with the issuer URL, or AWS with the account ID. Set the attribute mapping google.subject = assertion.sub.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step3: IAM and admin › Service accounts › Create service account, named bemmoly.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step4: Back on the pool, choose Grant access › Grant access using service account impersonation, pick the bemmoly account and "All identities in the pool", then Save.
pipelinesSetup.wif.step5: In the "Configure your application" dialog, pick the provider, enter the token path on Bemmoly's server, and Download config. That JSON is the file to choose here.
pipelinesSetup.wif.commandsLabel: Commands that make the workload identity file
pipelinesSetup.wif.fillIn: Type the project ID and number to fill the commands in.
pipelinesSetup.home.title: Welcome, {name}
pipelinesSetup.home.intro: Bemmoly Pipelines is empty, and nothing runs until you set it up. Do these in any order.
pipelinesSetup.step.cloudText: Pick a provider and the projects Bemmoly may reach. Nothing is created in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.step.environmentsText: Name them, link a project to each, and set their order and rules.
pipelinesSetup.step.peopleText: Give each person a role. Make approval groups if you want approvals.
pipelinesSetup.step.servicesText: Connect GitHub and pick the services to deploy.
pipelinesSetup.step.pipelinesText: For each service: start empty, from a template, or from a file in your repository.
pipelinesSetup.step.templatesText: 4 built-in templates are ready. Add your own, and steps every pipeline must keep.
pipelinesSetup.on.title: What's switched on
pipelinesSetup.on.footer: Everything starts off. Turn on what you need, when you need it.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.title: Start over
pipelinesSetup.startOver.text: Removes every Pipelines record on this install: clouds, environments, services, pipelines, runs, versions, change requests, approval groups and roles. Work, Docs, people and your cloud itself stay as they are; nothing is deleted in your cloud.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.dialogText: This cannot be undone. Pipelines becomes a fresh install with the setup checklist.
pipelinesSetup.startOver.done: Pipelines is empty again. {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} removed.
